sections.teaching:
Professor Lancelot is nice and humorous. He used only Excel to teach.

In my opinion, he explained the concept not very clearly during the lecture. However, he is easy to approach after class or through email. He used many real-life examples and cases to help us, which I found pretty useful.

Overall a good and passionate professor, but need more self-studying and thinking to clear up the concepts.
sections.grading:
Individual Class Participation and professionalism    10%
Group Homework 10%
Bi-Weekly Quizzes 40%-Multiple Choice
Final Exam 40%-Multiple Choice

5 quizzes, extremely easy. The mean is close to the full mark.
3 group assignments, the TA will specify some questions to be done in the textbook. Marks for this part is not released. We were allowed to form groups by ourselves (5-6 people per group).
The final exam was very challenging, open book and open laptop. There were 10+ MCs and 7 mini-cases. The cases were all about regression models, the most difficult topic in this course.

Spend a lot of time to understand the concepts, and do not think you can find the answer immediately in the exam by looking at the slides and the textbooks.

I got all full marks in the quizzes, and the final exam mark was not released. Got an A.

I am pretty sure that everyone got similar marks on quizzes and homeworks. The final exam is the only way to differentiate you from the others.
sections.workload:
Pretty heavy course, not because of its quantity but difficulty.

Getting all credits in quizzes is mandatory, and just try your best to do well in the final exam.

sections.content:
The things taught in this course is actually quite hard.
Most of it requires you to spend time and understand the logic behind statistics.
I've never skipped a single class in ISOM2500, but I come to class every time clueless and I leave class confused.
You will feel confused, but it's normal, Professor Lancelot understands that you are confused.
He will guide you through the quizzes.
sections.teaching:
Professor Lancelot is a realistic and humorous instructor.
He does not use Python and Minitab and all the extra tools to make the content extra complicated.
He tries his best to explain the contents in the simplest way, to a point I felt like I was stupid to not be able to understand what he was talking about.
All you have to learn is some excel, how to use a calculator and some formulas in his slides.
If you come to class, he will give you a sneak peek of what will be tested in the quizzes.
Just don't be rude in class; don't come late, don't leave early, he really doesn't like it.
sections.grading:
4-5 Quizzes every once in a while - 40% - released
Finals (not easy at all) - 40% - not released
10% participation - not released
10% Assignment - not released

Despite the low transparency, Professor Lancelot will not give you a bad grade as long as you submit your assignments on time, come to class and do your studying on his slides.

I honestly do not remember most of the things that he taught in class, and I remember not knowing half of the questions in the final exams (40%). I mainly focused on studying the components he said was important during class.

Somehow I got a B+, how? I don't really know.
sections.workload:
Attendance not compulsory.
2-3 Group Assignments from the textbook.
As long as the workload is distributed well, you will be fine.

The quizzes and finals conducted open book, open notes, and open laptop. Just that you can't use the internet.
So make sure you understand everything before the quiz and finals; in my opinion, understanding everything he was trying to teach requires the greatest effort and attention.

And yes, all quizzes and finals are MC.

sections.content:
Basic statistics knowledge. Completely the same with IB Math.
Very easy to be honest, that is why most of the students get a very high mark in the exam.

"Part I. Introduction
Course Organization
- Course outline
- Data and Variation (Ch2 - Ch6)
• Types of data, §2.1,2.2,2.4
• Describing categorical data, §3.1-3.4
• Association between categorical variables, §5.1-5.2
• Describing numerical data, §4.1-4.4
• Association between numerical variables, §6.1-6.3, 6.5
Part II. Probability
- Probability Model (Ch7 - Ch9)
• Basic concepts of probability, §7.1-7.2
• Independence, conditional probability, §7.3, 8.1-8.3 • Radom variable, mean and variance §9.1-9.4
- Association between Two Random Variables (Ch10)
• Portfolios, joint probability, §10.1-10.2
• Dependence between random variables, §10.3
• Mean and variance of weighted variables, covariance, §10.4, 10.6 • Game I
—– Quiz I —– - Normal Probability Model (Ch12)
• Normal random variable and normal Model, §12.1-12.2 • Normal quantile plot, §12.3-12.4
Part III. Inference
- Sampling and Sampling Distributions (Ch13 - Ch14)
• Concepts of population, sample and sampling, §13.1-13.2 • Game II
• Sampling distribution, §14.1
- Standard Errors and Confidence Intervals (Ch15) • Confidence interval for μ, §15.1-15.4
• Determine the sample size, §15.5 - Statistical Hypothesis Testing (Ch16)
• Concepts, §16.1
• One sample z- and t- tests, §16.2 - 16.3
—– Quiz II —– Part IV. Linear Regression
- Simple Linear Regression Model (Ch19 - Ch21)
• Linear pattern of data, residual plot, §19.1-19.3,19.5,
• Nonlinear pattern of data and transformation, §20.1-20.4 • The model and conditions, §21.1-21.2
• Inference in regression, §21.3
• Prediction interval, §21.4
BUSINESS STATISTICS (ISOM 2500) (L3), FALL 2017 3
- Regression Diagnostics (Ch22)
• Detecting differences in variation, §22.1 • Outlier and influential points, §22.2
• Dependent errors and time series, §22.3"

sections.grading:
Assignment: 70%
Final: 30%

sections.content:

- Probability
- Confidence Interval
- Random Variable

sections.teaching:
The professor is very willing to help students, and is usually available to have appointments with to ask questions. He also holds optional tutorials before the exams and provides a lot of practice questions that are similar to the exam question types.
However, some may find his accent difficult to understand. Additionally, he may avoid more advanced question types (e.g. MBA level questions) that is provided in the practice questions, as he doesn't think it's necessary for us to learn it, which may limit your learning if you're interested in statistics.
Overall, a pretty good professor.
sections.grading: The exams are purely MC questions, and are non-cumulative. The mean and SD for this course is pretty high, as the questions in the exams and assignments are quite straightforward.
sections.workload: Workload is a little bit heavy, as the assignments are long question types, and would also require the usage of Excel. However, you may pair up with two more students for the assignments, and the questions are not too advanced and are easy to tackle if you understand what is being taught in class.

sections.content: The content is mainly about R coding and statistical analyzing. Most other ISOM2500 classes work on trivial business statistics such as sd, mean, bar charts, and so on, so in comparison, the material of our class is extremely difficult even without considering the R coding part. Since the professor it a Japanese, many of its contents are statistical concepts mainly focused by Japanese researchers. Also, the analysis we do in the assignments mainly focuses on social science and economics instead of actual business practice, and I guess this is because the professor is actually from the ECON department (not ISOM) and he used to teach at Hitotsubashi University (which focuses on social and economic studies) before he came to HKUST in 2017.
sections.teaching: The Japanese professor is nice but his heavy accent is a huge problem for understanding. Also, what he mainly do in class is reading his lecture notes and reciting what the textbook says. Yet, he is actually a nice person and is willing to answer your questions and is never impatient to repeat his answers several times. If you pay a lot of attention in class and ask him questions after class, you could probably understand his teaching (though I tried to and failed).
sections.grading:
Assignment: 70%
Final: 30%

The assignments are mainly about R coding. Yet, the assignments have unreasonably high means (something around 9/10) and to my suspect, this is because the TA gives out very general scores. I spent a lot of time working on the assignments to get full marks, while some of my friends got 7s and 8s with answers randomly guessed. This is very unfair for students that actually worked hard on the assignments.

As for the final exam, it is mainly about statistical concepts and quantitative reasoning. It consists of 3 parts: True or false (10%), calculations and formula proving (10%), and R code reading (10%). Strangely, the final exam had nothing to do with what we did in the assignments. The final exam is mainly derived from the lecture notes and it seems that the professor expects you to cram and memorize the everything from the 500 pages of powerpoints. Also, surprisingly, some of the questions on the final exam is exactly same as the ones on the mock exam, so it is unwise to skip the mock exam thinking that the actual exam will not have questions from the mock exam (which was exactly what I thought ugh).

As for me, I got an average of 96.67% (58/60) for my assignments and the final exam is not released. Eventually, I got a B+ overall. (WTF)
sections.workload: The workload is unbelievably heavy if you have no basic knowledge of R coding (and I suppose over 90% of our class don't). We usually have an assignment every 2~3 weeks and typically I have to spend 6~8 hours on each assignment to achieve a 10 or 9.5 out or 10. I spent about 16~18 hours cramming the lecture notes before the final exam. The only good news is that the professor did not take attendance (though I suspect he will for his later on classes) and during the latter half of the semester, only about 25 students showed up for his class (full attendance should be somewhere around 80) (and yes I actually counted).

sections.content:
A very applied and practical course which doesn't really focus on the theoretical aspect. Doesn't require rigorous mathematical manipulation. Business students should find it useful.

(Note: Content differs from professor to professor.)

 Descriptive Statistics
      Tabular and Graphical Methods
      Numerical Method
      Association between Variables
 Probability and Random Variables
      Probability
      Discrete Random Variables
      Continuous Random Variables
 Estimation
      Sampling Distribution
      Central Limit Theorem
      Confidence Interval
 Hypothesis Testing
      Z-test and t-test for Population Mean
      Z-test for Population Proportion
      Chi-square Test for Independence
 Simple Linear Regression
      Least Squares Estimation
      Residual Analysis
      Coefficient of Determination
      Hypothesis Testing for Significance
      Prediction Estimates
      Analysis of Variance (ANOVA)

The course may start off very easy but as it progresses, the level of difficulty increases exponentially. Thus, don't undertake this course too lightly simply because of the seemingly easy beginning.
sections.teaching:
Kris is a very enthusiastic professor. She explains the concepts in details, and she encourages active participation in class by giving us chance to raise or answer questions. One thing I really like is that she does not mind "wrong answers" in class, which certainly helps us avoid making the same kind of mistake again in the exams.

I highly encourage u to attend all the lectures to have a better understanding of the course materials.
sections.grading:
It's a very competitive course overall cuz they're always some very capable students getting really high marks in the exams. A few careless mistakes can KILL. So if u aim at an A-range then u've to work VERY hard, be SUPER careful and make sure u get full marks in participation. I got a minor slip in quiz 2 and ended up in an A.

Exams are generally conceptually focused, e.g. the distribution of a certain variable, the interpretation of confidence interval, etc., rather than mathematical manipulation. U're pretty much unlikely asked to perform tedious calculation in the exams.

 Assignments: 95.48%
 Participation: 10/10
Total: 94.55%

sections.workload:
There are a total of 4 group assignments accounting for 10% of the total grade and u're allowed to form a group with at most 4 students to finish the assignments. The assignments are pretty hard and most of them require the use of MiniTab (it's still okay to use Excel, but the procedure might become crazily tedious and complicated). The most frustrating thing is probably to check all the groupmates' work afterward cuz there are always some groupmates making careless mistakes in dealing with the numbers. DON'T be a deadline fighter - please set the internal deadline well before the submission deadline, or u're pretty much finished.

There's also another 10% for participation. To earn participation mark, you can either raise a question or answer her question in her lectures, and she'll give u a card that gives u 1% participation in each lecture. A total of 10 cards will give u full mark in participation. If u're a little bit shy, then u can participate in the 2 randomly assigned class games which account for 2% each. As soon as u attend the lecture that day u'll be able to participate. If u attend both games, then u only need a total of 6 cards to get full marks for participation.

Three assignments with around 20 questions in each assignment.
Students could pair up to the assignments.
Therefore, the workload was light

sections.content: Games are the only part of content with fun.
sections.teaching: Teaching is quite interesting but too fast.
sections.grading: Actually the number of classes I attended should be less than 10 in the whole semester, I did not really read back the notes and book. Yet, my professor allowed us to have open book as well as open emotes midterm and final, so all you need to do is to learn everything new during the exam by yourself, if you only want to get b range. daily quiz is simple but the professor seems no longer teaching.
sections.workload: Some group assignments are required but quite easy to finish. Quiz and games are required to attend throughout the semester.

sections.content:
Content before first mid term is quite elementary and boring (bar charts, pie charts, mean, box plots median etc); expect mean to be very high for first midterm.

Content after first mid term gets more a lot more interesting and a little harder; (standard distributions, t distributions, confidence intervals for populations and samples and linear regression). Look up for study material online (easy to find, just google). Mean tends to drop at 2nd mid term and final.
sections.teaching: His teaching is alright in lecture (not the best in my opinion but that's just me). However he is very willing to help after class if you want him to explain more in depth or ask any specific questions. Very enthusiastic and willing to explain when you book an appointment.
sections.grading: Got below mean on 1st midterm and 2nd midterm but above mean on final and still got B, so great grading i guess? All MC though so be careful...
sections.workload: Weekly group problem sets. Good for practice and revision and not too heavy.

sections.content: This course teaches several most basic statistic models. They will help you to get the primary realization of the application of statistic in business world. But it won't mention too much about the reason behind the principle. It just care about whether you understand how to use it.
sections.teaching: The theories are not very easy to be mastered. Actually, it will be tough if you expect to study by yourself. But Dr.Pan is quite nice. She will repeat and explain them once and once again until you catch them. So it is crucial for your success to attend every class.
sections.grading: Grade is pretty nice. If you get a final grade higher than 95%, you will attain A plus.
sections.workload: Workload isn't much heavy. But you'd better review and  make your own notes in time after every lecture.

sections.content: Additional topics were taught in compare with other professors (e.g. Inference of two population means and variances).
sections.teaching: Teaching was fairly well but definitely not vivid. The Singaporean accent was a little obnoxious and hilarious sometimes. A point to note is his notes were well written, but it was essential to jot down notes in every lesson in order to obtain solutions for the questions in his notes for revision.
sections.grading:
Top 10% for A range.
Median grade is probably around C+.
sections.workload: Three problem sets. The last problem set was extraordinarily tough to complete. Note that a lot of questions required us to use Minitab software, which is not a free software we could obtain. We were supposed to complete the problems using the built-in Minitab in campus barn.

sections.content:
Quite easy at first, mainly some basic maths concept but totally different after the midterm. It takes much more time to understand the content after than before.
Instructor focused on the logic behind instead of calculation.
sections.teaching: Very difficult to follow. His pronunciation and the distorted meaning in the materials make revision much harder to finish.
sections.grading: Not much difference with the others.
sections.workload: Five assignments in total, not much reading materials. Assignments are handed in individually. Contents are entirely different from midterm questions, so not much reference in those assignments.

sections.content: Before the first midterm, the contents are all very easy. You can learn it by yourself easily. But after the second midterm, it feels like you choose the hell mode.
sections.teaching: He can remember everyone after the first class (if  you attend).He try to let every student gets involved to his teaching. You can stop him anywhere if you have questions, but if you sneak off, he will ask you questions immediately.
sections.grading: He is one of the most famous grading killer in ISOM. You sometimes only can get an A even if you are the first one in the total ranking (I don't know if he gave a A+ before). Also small A/B range.
sections.workload: Only three assignments in group with plenty of time after class. The first two were very easy, just need to follow the steps he taught in class.The third one is a little bit hard but not so challenging, which take about two hours after class.

sections.teaching:
explains concepts clearly and give lots of example
willing to answer questions during and after lessons
sections.grading:
good grade, I have one quiz below mean but still a range
use cards to count participation, have to answer 6 questions in the semester, but you can also get the card by asking question
sections.workload: 4 group assignments and you need to use statistics software minitab to finish it. A little bit difficult to use minitab but they will provide lab to teach you how to use. Don't try to do one assignment per person, it will spend you at least 2 hours even you understand the learning materials.

sections.content: Her notes are quite clear and useful for the assignments. The quizes and exams are related with the notes.
sections.teaching: Pretty interesting and provides students a lot of time to ask Qs. Having some games for the participation part and giving some prizes (usually chocolate) after the games and at the last class.
sections.grading: Basically dependent on the quizes and the exams, while it is a little hard to have the full participation mark.
sections.workload: Kris PAN will give you enough time to complete the assignents. The solutions of the assignments always can be found in the notes.

sections.content: Prof. WAN uses Python to teach statistics, making the course fascinating for those who love programming. I think it can even serve as an introductory course for programming if you dig deeper. Python is a very popular tool for data analytics these days, so it should be very useful. The assignments and exams are completely open-book and relatively easy. If you're interested in programming, never hesitate to take this course!
sections.teaching: Prof. WAN has a typical mainland Chinese accent, but it won't be a problem once you get used to it. He also makes a video for every lecture, so you don't need to attend. By the way, he is a very interesting man with a sense of humor.
sections.grading:
The grading is generally very good. There are 4 group assignments making up 50% in total. The Midterm and Final exam account for 20% and 30% respectively.
However, you need to be extremely careful, because most assignments and exams are too easy, which means everyone gets good scores. Even a small mistake can be a disaster.
The final exam is much more difficult than the previous tests, so you need to struggle for a good result. As it's completely open-book, a nicely prepared cheat sheet can help a lot.
sections.workload: The workload is very light. All four assignments are group assignments and very easy, you can do them in turns. The Midterm is also incredibly easy. Though I did not spend a single minute preparing for the Midterm (because I was busy with LANG 1002), I still got 99 out of 100. Only the Final requires some preparation, but I think it's natural for any course.

sections.content: I think the content is relatively easy as it includes total 5 topics and 2 of them are just basic probability concepts. The remaining 3 are relatively advanced concepts on regression models which are difficult to understand during the lesson and you have to study for few times after lessons to make sure yourself know what is doing as these 3 topics are highly related.
sections.teaching: Teaching is average , but you need to take lectures as the online lecture notes are not completed version. the lecturer will upload the complete version of lecture notes after few classes
sections.grading: There are totally 2 midterms,  one final exam, 10 participation card and 4 group assignments. I think the mean is pretty high as I exceed mean in two mid-terms and higher than a half SD in final, got 7 out of 10 participation cards, finished group assignments in relatively well performance.I think the mean is pretty high as I got 83% overall and my grade is B.
sections.workload: The workload is relatively heavy I think. There are totally 4 group assignments and each assignment includes about 8 questions related to the topic. Once you miss the lesson or the topic and then you won't know how to finish the assignment if you don't revise the lecture notes. It forces you to study so I think this is still good for your study.

sections.content: The content is quite simple comparing with other professors' teaching materials. Many of them involve calculation. Therefore, repetitive calculations could get a better result.
sections.teaching: Professor is nice and the learning environment is quite good.
sections.grading: Students have to get an extremely high score (>90%) in order to achieve A-range. As the course content is quite straight forward, it is a common phenomenon that students can get high scores. A minor mistake may lower the grading (around 1%).
sections.workload: The workload is a bit heavy. There would be a few assignments, quizzes, in-class participation and final exam.

sections.content:
教既野其實唔難,難係在於你要係教過既無數條式之中搵條正確既計出黎。
第一次MT考下你點計D中學野:graph再加少許conditional probit
第二次MT 係Normal distribution, Poisson distribution, binomial dist, 果堆既inferential statistics  
最後就係final, hypothesis testing 同埋 regression line.
有諗住考埋multiple regression 既但唔夠時間教就冇考到。2次MT同FINAL都係MC 形式, Mt 30條,FIANL 40條
sections.teaching: 每次教完一條新既式都有練習, 佢會DEMO比我地睇, 所以都幾易明,然後走堂真係自己蝕底。但上堂唔好傾計,一定比佢DIU, 佢D 英文都幾難聽,要D時間習慣下
sections.grading:
因為教D野簡單,勁多人高分
冇記錯個%好似係咁:
12% assignments
40% final
24% 1st mt
24% 2nd mt
然後76-80%都係B-
sections.workload: 有3份assignment, 一次15-20題左右, 1group 人做既, 每group最多3個人, 冇乜workload, 但有陣時要用Software 做,所以可以上tutor學下點用, 但唔上都得既,個software 唔難用。

sections.content: Even though the course is about Business Statistics, the main focus seems to be Python. The professor focuses more on trying to teach the programming language and spent almost 1.5 months on trying to teach that.
sections.teaching: The professor is very nice and extremely approachable. He tries to make classes fun but sometimes he is not able to communicate efficiently. He tries to connect what he is teaching to real life examples but this often leads to him going off topic. He posts his lecture videos and notes online so there is no need to attend each and every class.
sections.grading: The grading was surprising as the marks given for assignments and exams were pretty high but the final grades were mostly in the C- to B+ range.
sections.workload: The workload is light and included group assignments, a mid-term and a final. Group assignments have the highest weightage so if you have good group mates it should not be a problem. The mid-term and final were both "open everything" as you could refer to your notes and even use Google to try and find the answers.

sections.content:
The course includes:
descriptive Statistics
probability
random variable
confidence interval
hypothesis testing
simple linear regression
sections.teaching:
The lecture notes are very clear.
She is able to answer most of the question after the lecture.
sections.grading:
The grading includes:
four group assignments (10%)
two quizzes (40%)
participation (10%)
Final exam (40%)

There are only MC in the quizzes and the final exam.
If you ask or answer her a question during the lecture, she will give you a card. Each card contains 1 point. If you get 10 cards, you will get full marks in participation marks.
sections.workload:
The workload is not too much.
Only four group assignments in the whole semester.
It is quite easy.

sections.content: At first, Mr Wan's course is a little bit weird for me because he is the only professor who uses python to teach ISOM 2500. However, when you finish this course, you will find it really useful and unique. For the first month, he will teach you some basic functions of ipython notebook and for the rest of the course, you will use python to learn and solve business statistical problems. What is most interesting about this course is that Mr Wan hardly sticks to his plan, for he always leaves behind :)
sections.teaching: Mr Wan will get the notes ready before each class and he will do in person demonstration in class, so it's not to hard to catch up with what he teaches. Also, he is a really nice guy, he will patiently reply to your email and answer your questions after class.
sections.grading: Not that good. The grading includes four group assignments, mid-term and final. You may get a really low grade for a trivial mistake in the assignment. If you are familiar enough with python and the business concepts, you will get a good grade.
sections.workload: The workload is not too much if you really understand what is taught in class and do in-time review.

sections.content:
This class covers statistic concepts, calculations, as well as minitab skills.
PAN offers detailed slides and answers, which can be good material for review before quizzes and the final exam.
Minitab skills will be taught in extra lab sessions and tested in the quizzes. It's better to know how to use the software.
sections.teaching:
PAN is sweet and breezy. The classes are interesting.
PAN can speak cantonese and putonghua, and she will give out chocolates for games.

PAN will ask students to ask or answer questions in class to get cards for the participation grade. And it's better not to miss the games.
sections.grading:
Assignments 10% of Final (4 of them)
Quizzes  40% of Final (2 of them, 20% each)
Participation 10% of Final
Final Exam 40% of Final

No attendance will be taken but PAN requires students to get cards for participation grades.

Around 20% A range.
In my class top 5 got A+ and top 10 got A.
sections.workload:
Personally I don't feel the assignments are very resonable.
Because 4 group assignment with average 5-8 big questions in each have a strict requirement for teamwork. However this is only 10% in the final grade so a few students will not take it very seriously.
Maybe the workload is a little heavy for 10%.

sections.content: The lectures are easy up to the second midterm. Between the second midterm to the final, it gets harder and harder.
sections.teaching:
His teaching is fine, but you still need to revise some parts on your own; especially if you have never studied statistics before.
He hands out participation cards which would be beneficial for your marks.
sections.grading:
As long as you come to his lectures, you will surely score well in his tests.
There are 2 mid terms and the final exam is non-cumulative.
sections.workload: There are just 3 graded homeworks throughout the course of the semester.

sections.content: I took AP STAT and 80% of the material were repetitive. We got to regression towards the end and it got really difficult to understand but few days before the finals he announced that he's getting rid of the multiple regression part
sections.teaching:
Amazing professor
He's really nice and teaches amazingly
Careful with phone usage -- phones going off during class seriously pisses him off
sections.grading:
As long as you don't make silly mistakes you should be fine
You get to bring in one page of A4 cheat sheet (double-sided) during the exam
sections.workload: HW every so often but you can do it in a group. As long as you don't procrastinate til the last minute it should be fine

sections.content:
Basic statistical concepts, leading to inferential statistics and regression at last.
Basics of Minitab software is also covered by the lecturer, presumably to follow late trend of using computer to do needed calculations. Nevertheless, you are not required to know much about it.
sections.teaching:
Fairly passionate about the subject.
Always eager to answer questions from students.
Cares a lot about overall mood of the classroom, hates distracters.
sections.grading:
Grading of Mr.CHEN is notorious for not giving out good grades.
3 Assignments (that you may form a group up to 3) : 12%
2 Midterms : 48%
1 Final exam : 40%
Reflecting overall grading plan, I assumed myself to be at top 25~30% of the class and got B+.
I would say it was not that bad, considering all the stories about his ruthlessness.
sections.workload:
Unless you tend to procrastinate a lot, you will not be overwhelmed by workload of the lecture.
Just be prepared for the exams using slides (and hopefully questions on the textbook), as they contain some tricky questions.

My complain is that I had to purchase a costly textbook just because I need it to do my assignment.

sections.content:
Content is standardized.
Business core course and content was not really hard, quite similar to high school mathematics course actually.
sections.teaching: If you can understand the accent and slightly fractured English, it will be alright. Sometimes the professor doesnt explain the concept very well, but being able to compute and understanding it yourself with notes and practices will be fine.
sections.grading: Full marks on both midterms, above one sd in finals, A grade.
sections.workload:
2 group assignments, self assigned group.
WOrkload is not really high and just understand the concepts well and do know how to compute for the examinations.

sections.content:
Data analysis using python (programming).
Those who have studied python will find it very easy to follow and get high mark becasue it teaches a lot of basic python code.
It also teach probability, estimation, distribution and regression, it may be easier for who have studied M1 to handle.
sections.teaching: It is not clear enough because the professor just key in some code and only explain a little, it is difficult to understand the content.
sections.grading: quite good because professor is trying his best to give good grade.
sections.workload:
4 group assignments.
1 mid-term and 1 final.

sections.content:
Covers basic statistics

Limited syllabus (cover way fewer topics than other professors) that students without any stats background can easily fit into the course

Uses python as teaching and exam tools, it adds extra requirement on students who are not familiar with coding

Personal Comment:
It is interesting to use python as the teaching medium as python is the tool used frequently in real-life business data analysis.
Wan Xuhu is the only professor who takes this approach, all other professors stick with the conventional ways, pen, paper and calculator (cheatsheets as well).

If you have limited knowledge on coding, try to learn it or find a friend who is capable to "hard carry" you. Otherwise, you should not choose this lecture.

Do NOT rely on Prof himself or TA for coding problems as it is just very inconsistent.
sections.teaching:
Despite he is a nice guy, there are trolls everywhere
He makes mistakes constantly and is unable to correct them
(Multiple mistakes are found in his solutions on practice exams)

Students can totally skip ALL the lectures but remember to check out ALL lecture notes to know the topics required then learn them yourself

Make good use of online resources like Wikipedia, Khan Academy, etc.

Do NOT try to ask him questions on coding, just Google them yourself or ask your friends
He shows little understanding on coding concepts and barely gives explanations of his codes clearly

In short, he writes bad codes
(any UST CS students may perform better than him in coding)
sections.grading:
50% group assignments (in groups of 1-4)
20% midterm
30% final

Grades are scaled within lectures ONLY (as he is in-charge of 2 lectures in Fall 2016)

Both exams are completely OPEN-EVERYTHING (including network, but ofc you should not try to communicate with your friends, this is counted as cheating)

Easy A-range for students without great stats background but adequate understanding on coding (knowledge on statistics is still required, but not that intensive relative to other professors)

Average performance went horribly wrong in the final for some unknown reasons, given 60% of the exam questions are exactly the same (even decimals are not changed) as Final Fall 2015

Midterm: mean=86/91, SD=10.5/9.5
Final Exam: mean=52-53, SD=23

On rough estimation, mean of overall mark should be around 81-84%
Though I got great results at the end, overall grading is a bit tight, 88.X% leads to B (high) / B+ (low), so I cannot give an A to grading

A+ (overall 94.9%, 100% on all assignments)
sections.workload:
Extremely low workload if you have either good understanding on coding or good group mates

Assignments can be finished in minutes, single-handedly
You can totally "free-ride" your group mates without causing any troubles to them

Do spend time to understand basic concepts of coding (for students without any experience) and learn to read error messages and fix the problem on your own

sections.content: P-value, probability, simple regression model are not that hard to understand and handle. Some statistics videos in Youtube would make the concepts clearer.
sections.teaching: Disastrous. His mainland accent and teaching direction confused us. Not a single of us could understand what he was trying to explain. Lots of misspellings in his Powerpoint and you should expect that you can learn nothing from his lectures and powerpoints
sections.grading: Bad. 3 times above mean with a 90% homework score ended up B-. I don't quite understand how could his grades be so poor. I regretted registering his lectures.
sections.workload: Homework not hard at all, with a group in 3. There were only 3 homework sets throughout the semester.

sections.content: The slides provided are not very clear without the assistance of the textbook. Yet since the course is not accumulative, the final exam is only based on 2 chapters. Practice papers and review sessions were also given before midterm/final exam.
sections.teaching: Poor English and students usually find it very challenging to stay focused in his class. Most students just use their laptops for other uses.
sections.grading: I achieved 90% overall with my final exam being above mean of 1.16SD (38/40) and got B+ at the end. I also know people with their finals being above mean getting B-.
sections.workload: 3 group assignments and 2 midterms. Attendance was taken 4 times randomly, each accounted for 1% of the course.

Basic Python
Most frequent word"handsome"

sometimes noisy

sections.grading:
Grading:(all by python)

Group assignments (maximum member size=4): 50%

Midterm (in class): 20%

Final: 30%
sections.workload:
Totally 4(or 5) group assignments and all that means is basically gatherings with your teammates and spending about an hour and a half time to finish 2-5 questions taught  in class.
Mid-term and Final you just need to know copy and paste(but you need to know what you are doing and how the combination can lead to the results needed.

sections.content: Content is relevant to real life circumstances and course teaches you how to apply basic statistics to daily life. Also teaches how to use the Minitab software (statistics software which is more useful than Excel) for real data acquired from daily life problems.
sections.teaching: Teaching is very clear as he uses a lot of examples that helps you understand the material more. Good pronunciation and also provides detailed lecture notes. You would only need to learn from his lecture notes as it is already very clear. Teacher is very friendly and remembers student's names.
sections.grading: Not bad considering his exams are similar to the problem examples he did in class so its not very hard and the mean is not that high as well. For the first midterm, the mean is 46/60 and it drops to 44/60 on the second midterm.
sections.workload: Gives 3 problem sets throughout the entire course and the problem gets harder as we get closer to the end of the semester. But its a group assignment so you can divide the workload. No other assignments except the problem set.

sections.content: The first few chapters are really easy especially for mainland students because the content is included in their high school classes.
sections.teaching: Very clear. Pan won't go too fast. She'll explain everything in detail. And she's also trying to be funny and interesting. She's from mainland so she can speak Chinese and Cantonese and English pretty well.
sections.grading: very fair
sections.workload: OK. Four assignment with a four people group, two quizes that allow cheat sheet and one final. The assignment is not difficult. There are three lab sessions you can attend voluntarily. But they are really helpful for your assignment. Two quizzes are all Mutiple Choice questions.

sections.content: Content is sufficient, but doesn't follow a certain book. I believe the book and supplementary information is needed to do well on the quizzes. There are 3 quizzes, 3 assignments and 5% of the grade belongs to participation in class. 3 assignments are easy because they are the practice quizzes given before the actual quizzes (just answer and show work for a few questions assigned).
sections.teaching: Professor is very passionate about teaching, and is very nice as he takes the time to get all his students involved. But it's quite hard to understand him in class. At times his explanations are clear, but other times his explanations can be unclear.
sections.grading: Grading of assignments are very generous. Can't say much about the grading of quizzes, as there is only one correct answer for MC.
sections.workload: Workload is not too heavy. All assignments he gives are a few questions from the practice quizzes he gives out before each quiz.

sections.content: Relatively simple content related to business statistics - focuses on general statistical methods, probability, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, etc. The content is well summarised on the lecture slides, however it's not complete so it's wise to go to class because she mentions a lot of extra information in class that isn't on the slides.
sections.teaching: Kris is a really clear teacher, and she's very patient when answering questions. Although she might have a slight accent, it's pretty easy to understand her so it should be no problem trying to follow her in class. She's also really nice if you approach her before/after class with questions.
sections.grading:
Grading is pretty fair, but a warning - the mean is pretty high!

There are 2 quizzes and a final exam (all are non-cumulative, but you do need some of the previous content in later topics - e.g. confidence intervals in hypothesis testing etc). The quizzes have 25 questions, and you are allowed a double-sided handwritten cheat sheet. The mean is pretty high, so try to be 1 SD above mean.

There are also 4 homework assignments which you complete in a group. The questions are pretty decent but a bit tricky, however do review these questions because the exam questions are a bit similar.

Kris also gives out participations cards, and there are also 2 games during the semester which count for participation credit.
sections.workload: Not too much workload, depending on how much time you're willing to invest in the course.

sections.content: Mostly about basic statistic concepts and a little bit minitab knowledge. Questions in exams are quite straightforward, but are required to fully understand the concepts. It's not difficult to follow if you pay attention in class.
sections.teaching: Kris explains every details about the concepts in class well. Her slides are well-written with adequate examples to show you how to do the calculations. But you still need to take some notes. You can ask her questions in Cantonese, Mandarin, or English. Overall she is a nice lecturer.
sections.grading:
Questions in exams are relatively easy to other lecturers. Calculations are too easy. Questions that asking about concepts sometimes may be difficult. You need to fully understand every terminology.
So getting an A-range is quite competitive. The mean is high. Since there are participation cards that are worth of 10%, it's important to get full marks in participation if you want an A-range grade. You can probably get an A/A+ when the total grade =>95%.
But if you just aim for an average grade, it would be easy.
sections.workload: Workload is very low. You just need to do 4 group assignments throughout the whole semester. There are 2 midterms and 1 final but non-cumulative.

sections.content: Requires understanding of programming (Python) but the actual statistics part is not very hard. Had many classmates coming out of every class not knowing what he was talking about and copying down wrong codes
sections.teaching: Prof. Wan is very humorous and nice. Teaches things outside of the syllabus and shares personal experience in the finance industry.
sections.grading:
Final was above mean 0.65 SD

Got full marks for all assignments

But still got a B...

What is this...
sections.workload: Workload is not heavy at all. As long as you know what you're doing, the 5 group assignments (accounting for 50% of the grade) will no take very long.

sections.teaching: It took me a bit time to understand and get used to professor's accent, yet he is a passionate in teaching and willing to answer your questions.
sections.grading: The mean of the course is quite high.
sections.workload: Quite light, only need to submit 3 assignments but he had come across those question. You have to get four participation cards so as to gain all the participation credits.

sections.content: Content is comparably easy and does not require to memorise the content as it allows to use cheat sheet. All exams are non-cumulative.

Also, try to be more active during classes, answer or ask her questions will both help, as she requires students to get 10 participation cards. sections.content: Great and organized content, he has 4 main topics , each divided to 2/3 sub-contents. Content is easy to understand and required basic math knowledge.

sections.grading:

sections.content: There was plentiful content on how to get equipped for using statistics in business situations with examples such as linear regression.

sections.grading:
There were 5 or 6 group assignments and they had a very strict grading , but the quizzes and the final exam are all MC questions and although very hard are solvable provided you attend all lessons as similar problems will be discussed during class.
(p.s. I do not have the exact data but a B can be easily attained without much effort)
sections.workload: Very little workload. The materials are not hard to follow if you attends the lecture. Because of the introductory nature of the course, it is very easy to catch up even if you miss some lectures in a row.

sections.content: Content was ok. First he taught a lot of basic stuff about business statistics including mean, mode, standard deviation, etc. Then he went on with more complex stuff like confidence intervals, samples.

He often just read off the presentation slides, so might as well stay at home and read it yourself since it saves u time and workload. He didn't really take attendance, so don't worry about that.
sections.grading: Grading was fair.
sections.workload: Work load was average, just 4 homework in total, which was easy at first, then harder when it got to the later teaching materials.

sections.content: This course is about statistic and some of the content is already learnt in the secondary school. But there are also some new and more complicated knowledge about statistic.
sections.teaching: The content is well-explained. The professor will do some of the example with you step-by-step. He is open to questions and is also an interesting person which make the lecture less boring.
sections.grading: 48% of the grade come from two midterms and another 40% come from one final which are all mc. No attendance is needed to be taken. There is no participation mark. The other 12% is from the 3 problem sets.
sections.workload: The workload is very light. Only three problem sets are needed to be done during the whole semester. You can form a group of two to three to hand in the problem sets together or you can finish them by yourself. Forming a group can help to reduce your workload.

sections.content: it is said to be the easiest content among other instructors in isom2500. All stuffs are taught via powerpoint, no other teaching materials are needed, twice gaming section per semester. It should not be difficult for those who have studied M1 in secondary school. Maths knowledge is required (specially in form of concepts) but those maths question in exam can be solved by equation its proved even you do not understand the concept of it at all.
sections.teaching: Pretty straight forward teaching following the flow of the powerpoint with some funny (not that much actually) examples. Really nice to those having questions to ask. So feel free to ask more questions and most of the time she can explain it better than what she talked during the lessons.
sections.grading: Tests are in mc only, students usually get a high mean score which maybe a drawback, but overall recommended for those who aims for high grade. Providing a score system that requiring students to answer questions during the lesson, which is actually a chance for students to score high grade since some of them usually wont even attempt once.
sections.workload: Workload is acceptable, maybe group assignments every one to two weeks and thats all. The assignments from the first half semester is pretty easy to do but those after the mid-term test can be challenging, the mean score of the assignments are usually high, which should beware of.

sections.content: Really interesting stuff. It feels like you can actually apply the knowledge you have gained. The course material really varies between professors.  Everything is write here is about Prof James.
sections.teaching:
Prof James is really good and has really interesting teaching style.  He emphasizes real life application, you don't have to remember any formulas by heart.

You don't have to attend the lectures, but some powerpoint slides might be confusing.
sections.grading:
It's good. There are 3 quizes that are super easy (8/10 is the mean) and the final that is quite hard. You gotta go through all the powerpoint slides. Many questions are exact copies of the ones that are shown in the PPT.

There is also a participation grade, but I think nobody ever got any points for that.

You are allowed to bring EVERYTHING to the exam, even your laptop, but you don't get internet connection.  This makes the exams different. Some people may not like it. It favors thinking over memorization.
sections.workload: Not too much. You can "half learn" everything as you can access the  laptop during your exam.

sections.content: prof. Pan is a great teacher. Her lectures are punctual, clear and not so difficult. Shes willing to answer students' questions after lecture.
sections.teaching: The teaching pace is just about right, wont be so fast even for students with medium math bg. Its better to preview the lecture notes before lesson cause u need to ans some of the questions in the lecture note to obtain the card.
sections.grading: There are 2 quizzes and 1 final. All of them are MCs only and you may find them not so difficult if you pay attention on class and do the exercises assigned by TA. Students also need to answer questions to get the card (instead of taking attendance)  which weigh 10% of the overall marks.
sections.workload: The workload is not so heavy, just 4 groupworks throughout the whole course. Normally, students will be given around 1 week to finish the groupworks which are difficult indeed even if you pay attention on lecture.

sections.content: Basic business statistics

sections.workload: Even though there are 3 quizzes and 3 assignments, these are pretty trivial, so I would say workload is low.

sections.workload: The project may require a lot of workload... Best thing is you don't need to worry about exams. Just a couple of hours of review, and you can understand the concepts. (but i still dunno how to get high marks:)

sections.grading: Attendance, 2 quizzes(midterms), 4 assignments and 1 final. Compared to other professors Kris gives very good grades as far as I know. Usually above mean less than one sd and finally got A-

sections.content:
In this course there are 2 midterms and 1 final.
The material for the first midterm is about basic probability and some statistics theory.
The second midterm covers about normal distribution and confidence interval.
And the final covers about linear regression and hypothesis testing.
sections.teaching: As an international student, I find it really hard to understand what he is saying. I came only to his first two lectures and it was useless for me. However, he does try his best to make sure everybody understand the material and answer to all of his students questions.
sections.grading:
The grading is really good ( just like most of ISOM 2500 professors I think ).

24% Midterm 1 ( mean : around 19/24 )
24% Midterm 2 ( mean : 14/24 )
40% Final ( mean : 23.5 / 33 )
12% Assignment ( there are 4 assignments )
sections.workload:
The exams are not cumulative and we can bring 2 sided A4 cheat sheet so we do not have to memorize any formulas. Plus, if we come to the last lecture before any of the exams, Du Lilun will tell what will be tested.

The assignment is not hard as well. Each assignment have around 5 problems and we are given around 2 weeks to finish it. We can also form a group up to 3 people to do the assignment.

Overall, I think the workload is really light.

sections.content:
Probability, obviously that is something that you've learnt in your high school, so this one is easy.
Confidence interval, something new, but not as difficult as you think, read the material given for two days and you can understand it, at least how to solve the calculation questions in the midterm.
Hypothesis testing and Linear Regression......
insanely difficult!!!!!!!! It takes me about 3 days to have a little understanding on it!!! But when you read do more exercises and read the slides more often, you can ace it.
sections.teaching:
Dulilun's accent is.... completely not understandable..... He accent is too serious that I can barely understand, and I need to spend so many time in understanding his accent. So...I skipped the classes quite often, since even if I go, I will not pay attention, so I would rather skip the class to have a day-off lol.
(At the syllabus, there is no attendance, but Mr.Du thought that there are so many people skip his class, so he decided to take attendance, you might have a chance to upgrade from B+ to A- if you have full attendance, btw, it means you are the greatest among all the B+, which means you slightly a little bit less than A-, can have a chance for upgrading)
sections.grading:
23/24 mean 19

19/24 mean 14(I exclude the mark addition, Du thought that the grade of this midterm is so bad that he decided to add 4 point to each of us, which is completely useless..)

30/33 mean 23

some assignments both above mean

got A
sections.workload:
Four assignments one final and two midterms, quite a lot of things to do in fact. But I think there is no need for you to read the textbook, but practicing the questions would be useful.

A tip: REMEMBER TO UNDERSTAND THE CONCEPT!!! As a math-related courses, I used to think that there will be only calculation problems, but I was wrong.... So many tricky concept problems.

sections.teaching:
Dr. Pan teaches well, she understands what you will confuse and explain them in detailes, with tons of examples used.

Her lively tone makes the lesson less boring. Her presentation skills is really good, you can definitely understand the materials after she presents them to you. Each year, many students would like to swap in her lectures.

As long as you can get above 1 SD, or even a little bit lower, you can get an A range, but for A or A+, you need to get around 94-5% of the course total.

sections.content: All professors have a similar syllabus, but Prof. Kris Pan's sessions are easier than the other professors', as she tends to skip all the parts she finds "too difficult for year 1 students", while other professors may still cover those parts. Concepts such as standard deviation, variance, confidence interval and sample mean are highly favourable to students who have studied M1 in secondary school. Hypothesis testing about critical values and p-values is something new, but not difficult to understand as long as you practise more with the exercises in class and the homework questions. The most difficult topic, linear regression, was not assessed much in the final.
sections.teaching: Not much comment about the teaching.
sections.grading:
Simply to say, it is extremely easy to get a B+, but if you want to get A range, it is not easy at all.

Most of the students get a B+ in Kris Pan's session as her quizzes and exams are extremely easy with only straight-forward multiple choice questions. A one page, double-sided cheat sheet is allowed, so as long as you copy all the important information from the ppts on to the cheatsheet, you can easily score above 80%. However, since the scores of students are packed together, any careless mistake may cause you to follow below the mean, so make sure you do not get more than 3 questions wrong in any of the papers if you want to get at least a B+.

The differentiating point between B+ and A range is during the final, where there are 3-5 questions you cannot directly find the answer or required concept from the ppts. In this case, it depends on whether you have been paying attention in class and have jogged down some points that the professor has mentioned but did not appear in the slides.

I only got a B+ in the end and my total score for the whole course was 93/100. To get an A range you probably need to get 95/100, which means you need to get almost everything correct.
sections.workload: Aside from 2 midterm quizzes and a final, there are group homework sets every 2/3 weeks. The homework is not difficult, but be sure to proofread and check the answers for your group mates as well. Many times students divide the questions among the group and only focus on their own question, so there may be some errors as a result.

sections.content:
Essentially, the course is divided into four aspects ranging from simple descriptive statistics, to probability & distributions, regressions, and hypothesis testing.

Content is generally easy to follow, and in the case that you don't, the professor is very willing to repeat things in class and/or respond to your queries via email.

You may find like you aren't getting enough practice questions, so feel free to approach him, and he will suggest some for you to do.
sections.teaching:
Great professor, with a real love for statistics. Engages the class often, and will go through every line of text in his notes during the lectures. Feel free to ask questions at any point during the lecture if it seems confusing to you.

He is very structured in his teaching, punctual, responsive via email, and has a zero-tolerance attitude for anyone disturbing his teaching. Don't be surprised when he goes completely mute and stares at one person, because they're in trouble! Don't use your phone in class, and don't talk loudly, and you'll be fine. Don't be surprised to find out that he knows your name, even though you've never spoken in class.

Hands down, one of the most passionate profs I've had classes with.
sections.grading:
The grading for this course is very objective - exams (midterm and final) are MCQ based, and problem sets have fixed answers.

The means for all exams tend to be quite high, such that sometimes the max a person can get is 0.7 to 0.8SD above mean. That being said, it's easy to mess up, because everything is MCQ based. He will allow you to use a cheatsheet during all exams.

2 Midterms, 24% each
3 Problem sets, 4% each
1 Final, 40%

No official attendance, but it seems like he takes it mentally. Friend of mine received the same scores as me for almost all assessments, and finished a subgrade below.

Don't worry about where you stand during the course. He is a statistics professor, and will provide you every single statistic you can think of for the midterms (I remember him uploading a 12 page document full of midterm related statistics).
sections.workload: A problem set a month, a midterm every month and a half. Nothing excess about the workload of this course, but keep in mind, that to do well, you would ideally want to do some practice problems in your free time, so that you ensure you're actually retaining the knowledge from his classes.

Kris teaches interactively. She would engage with the entire class through her gestures and often ask questions to students.

She would use some simple illustrations/examples to open the topic of each lesson so to introduce/recap on some materials.

One minor point is that she really hate people talking in her class. She would get annoyed by that quite quickly.

Class participation is fun actually. Just fire questions / answer questions during the class to earn participation points.
sections.workload: The workload for the course is okay. Just don't skip too many classes and you will be fine.

Workload is not large. It is really important you attend all his lessons. In the midterms/finals there are questions which are not exactly related to ISOM but more to specific examples he showed in lessons. Also, in order to get answers to PPT slides you must go to class to listen to him.

There are only two midterms and one final which are all non-cumulative. Occasionally there is homework, but it is really easy to do.

sections.teaching: Professor explains his notes clearly. He's willing to answer students' questions.
